decisions.question: OQ-R2, first half (Guide §10.1 'Envelope recording'): what is the envelope recorder's assertion API: pattern matching, equality, custom predicates?

options.label: typed queries returning plain values
options.consequence: envelopes, envelopesOf(topic) and payloadsOf(topic) return unmodifiable lists typed by the topic; tests use ==, Dart 3 patterns and Iterable.where with their runner's expect; no new dependency; failure messages are whatever expect prints

options.label: package:matcher matchers over envelopes
options.consequence: richer failure messages (isEnvelope(payload: ..., source: ...)), but nidana_dart_runtime gains a dependency that ADR-002 item 3's table and bus-api@v1 G39 do not list, so a bus-api amendment and a runtime D{n} would follow

options.label: a predicate DSL of its own
options.consequence: a vocabulary to learn and maintain that Dart patterns already cover

decisions.why: Dart 3 already gives equality, destructuring patterns and predicates over values, so the recorder only has to hand out typed values; the cast from MessageEnvelope<Object?> to the topic's type is the one thing tests cannot write conveniently, and envelopesOf/payloadsOf do it. Deterministic ids and the fixed initial time (G13) make whole-envelope equality usable. The owner's preference for values and composition over DSLs points the same way, and the runtime's dependency set stays as ADR-002 and bus-api@v1 G39 fix it. Signal that would change it: app teams writing the same envelope matchers in several test suites; matchers can then ship as a compatible addition in a separate library.

decisions.question: OQ-R2, second half (Guide §10.1 'Topology test isolation'): how does a test activate only the topologies under test without the APPLICATION set?

options.label: TestBus activates nothing; input and stub helpers stand in for absent producers
options.consequence: isolation is the default; TestBus.input (a publisher of ServiceSource('test')) and TestBus.stub(topic) (a writer claiming one state topic at application scope) replace the boilerplate every test would write; two more members and one guarantee

options.label: documented pattern only, no helpers
options.consequence: smallest surface; every test constructs its own publishers and claims, as bus-api@v1's live binding does by hand

options.label: a selective activation API over an app bootstrap
options.consequence: a TestBus that runs the app's bootstrap and ignores activations not listed; couples tests to the bootstrap and hides which topologies are active

decisions.chosen: TestBus activates nothing; input and stub helpers stand in for absent producers
decisions.why: On this tree activation is always explicit (bus-api@v1 G22, G34): a fresh TestBus has nothing active, so the Guide's question reduces to standing in for the producers that are absent, as hsdd/spec/nidana.runtime.md's OQ-R2 detail already observes. The stand-in for a state topic must claim it (Spec §2.4, §3.11), which is the boilerplate bus-api@v1's bus_activation_test.dart writes by hand; stub makes it one call, claims at Scope.application so it never trips the scope check, and claims one topic per publisher so stubs never conflict with each other. Close to the no-helper option; the signal that would change it is a consumer for whom a fixed ServiceSource('test') source is wrong.

decisions.question: Spec §9.2 item 2: the TestBus envelope recorder defaults to redacting sensitive payloads, raw view by explicit opt-in. Where does the opt-in live, given that bus-api@v1's bindings read recorder.envelopes and RecordedEnvelope.envelope?

options.label: per read: RecordedEnvelope.unredacted and an unredacted: true argument on the typed queries
options.consequence: envelope is unredacted.redacted(), so non-sensitive envelopes are the delivered objects and bus-api@v1's bindings work unchanged; typed queries on a sensitive topic throw ArgumentError without the argument; every raw read is visible at its call site

options.label: per recorder, a flag at TestBus construction
options.consequence: not expressible as a named parameter, because TestBus([BusConfig config]) already has an optional positional parameter and Dart cannot mix the two; would need a BusConfig field that bus-api@v1 owns

options.label: a separate raw view object (recorder.unredacted)
options.consequence: two parallel query surfaces to keep in step

decisions.chosen: per read: RecordedEnvelope.unredacted and an unredacted: true argument on the typed queries
decisions.why: The Spec asks for an explicit opt-in; a per-read opt-in is the most explicit form and keeps the default view redacted everywhere, including toString(), which is what a failing expect prints. topic-model@v1's redacted() returns the envelope itself when not sensitive (G15 there), so bus-api@v1's live binding, which casts non-sensitive envelopes to MessageEnvelope<T>, runs unchanged (T9 in the experiment). A construction flag is blocked by the TestBus signature the orchestrator fixed.

decisions.question: Does a TestBus generate deterministic envelope ids (bus-api@v1 says only that ids are opaque and pairwise distinct)?

options.label: deterministic with a fixed format: e1, e2, ... and c1, c2, ... per TestBus
options.consequence: whole envelopes are predictable with the fixed initial time, so a test can write an expected MessageEnvelope literally and compare two runs or two buses with ==; tests that hard-code ids break when an unrelated publish is added

options.label: deterministic, format unspecified
options.consequence: golden comparisons between runs work, literal expected envelopes do not

options.label: opaque, as on a production bus
options.consequence: nothing to state, but envelope equality is unusable in tests

decisions.chosen: deterministic with a fixed format: e1, e2, ... and c1, c2, ... per TestBus
decisions.why: Rationale §3.2 makes determinism the TestBus's point, and equality is one of the three assertion styles Guide §10.1 names; a fixed format is what makes equality on whole envelopes available. Distinctness within a bus, all bus-api@v1 G12 asks, still holds. Signal that would change it: a consumer relying on ids being unique across buses, which bus-api@v1 does not promise.

decisions.question: ADR-003 item 5 leaves the default start instant of the virtual clock to this contract. Which instant?

options.label: 2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z, overridable by initialTime
options.consequence: fixed, UTC, far from today so an accidental wall-clock read stands out; the ADR-003 prototype's value

options.label: the Unix epoch 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z
options.consequence: millisecondsSinceEpoch 0 is a common 'unset' sentinel in app code, so a timestamp at the epoch can be mistaken for a missing one

options.label: the wall clock at construction, as fake_async does
options.consequence: not deterministic across runs, against G13 and Rationale §3.2

decisions.why: Fixed and UTC is what determinism needs; 2000 avoids the epoch sentinel and was already exercised by docs/auto-run/experiments/virtual-scheduler/. No evidence distinguishes 2000 from other fixed instants; the choice is conventional.

decisions.question: ADR-003 items 5 and 6 leave the action bound and the settle bound to this contract. Which defaults, and where are they set?

options.label: constructor parameters maxActions = 100000 per operation and maxSettleTurns = 20 per settle
options.consequence: one place to configure a scheduler, shown by getters; bus-api@v1's harness calls settle() with no argument; a test with a long legitimate periodic timer raises maxActions on its scheduler

options.label: per-call arguments on each operation and on settle
options.consequence: more flexible per call, but the bounds become a parameter of every call site and the bus-api@v1 bindings could not pass them

options.label: no bounds
options.consequence: a microtask loop or a zero-period periodic timer hangs the test instead of failing it, against ADR-003 item 5

decisions.chosen: constructor parameters maxActions = 100000 per operation and maxSettleTurns = 20 per settle
decisions.why: The prototype values were exercised in docs/auto-run/experiments/virtual-scheduler/ and bus-api-fixtures; 100000 actions allows, for example, a 16 ms periodic timer over 26 minutes of virtual time in one advance, more than a topology test needs, and still fails a runaway loop within milliseconds. The signal that would change the default: a consumer's realistic test hitting the bound.

decisions.question: ADR-003 item 5: the scheduler 'reports how many are pending and when the next one is due'. What introspection does VirtualScheduler expose?

options.label: pendingTimerCount, nextTimerDue and pendingMicrotaskCount
options.consequence: a test asserts a cancellation by count and the next deadline by instant; quiescence (G9) becomes observable

options.label: pendingTimerCount only
options.consequence: what bus-api@v1's harness uses; the 'when the next one is due' half of ADR-003 item 5 would be missing

decisions.why: ADR-003 item 5 names both the count and the next due instant; the microtask count costs nothing and makes G9's quiescence checkable by a case.

decisions.question: ADR-003 item 6: the envelope recorder attaches to a bus with either provider. How does it attach to a production-provider bus, given that Bus is bus-api@v1's final class?

options.label: EnvelopeRecorder.attach(bus): a delivery seam of every bus, called before the observers
options.consequence: records Tracing.disabled and sensitive topics like TestBus.recorder, counts against no limit, adds no timer; needs a recorder seam inside Bus, which shares the src library anyway (bus-api@v1 Refinement 1)

options.label: a BusObserver with both capabilities, registered with addObserver
options.consequence: no seam in Bus, but it misses Tracing.disabled topics (bus-api@v1 G30), counts against maxObservers and sees deliveries after earlier observers, so a widget test's recording differs from a TestBus's

decisions.chosen: EnvelopeRecorder.attach(bus): a delivery seam of every bus, called before the observers
decisions.why: One recorder behavior on every bus keeps VM tests and widget tests comparable, and bus-api@v1's delivery rule already places the TestBus recorder before observers. The seam is internal to the shared src library. bus-api@v1's delivery-rule wording names 'the recorder of a TestBus'; an editorial alignment is listed in the notes.

decisions.question: Guide §6.5: the per-topic ordering regression test is mandatory and 'the test harness in nidana-test-utils provides it'. Does this contract expose a reusable harness, and where does the test run?

options.label: OrderingProbe in testing.dart, plus the runtime's own cases
options.consequence: an application runs the regression test on its own buses, under any provider (widget tests included); the runtime's gate runs bus-api@v1 G13 and this contract's G19 cases; one small type

options.label: no harness; bus-api@v1's G13 cases are the regression test
options.consequence: nothing new, but Guide §6.5 and Guide C.5 place the test in the test utilities that adopting teams use

options.label: a function that runs a whole regression test on a TestBus
options.consequence: self-contained, but tied to virtual time, so it cannot run in a widget test

decisions.chosen: OrderingProbe in testing.dart, plus the runtime's own cases
decisions.why: Guide §6.5 says the test utilities provide the harness and Guide C.5 lists it as v1 tooling teams verify their stack with; ADR-002 item 6 makes testing.dart those utilities. A probe that only subscribes and compares, leaving the publishing and time driving to the test, works under every provider.

decisions.question: How does the settle operation behave at its edges: where does it live, when does it fail, and what happens when it is called inside the scheduler's zone?

options.label: on VirtualScheduler; StateError at the call inside the zone; the future fails after maxSettleTurns real turns
options.consequence: buses sharing a provider settle once; a misplaced call fails loudly instead of hanging

options.label: on TestBus, failing asynchronously in every case
options.consequence: an async failure raised inside the scheduler's zone completes through a virtual microtask, so awaiting it from the test would never return unless something drains the queue

decisions.chosen: on VirtualScheduler; StateError at the call inside the zone; the future fails after maxSettleTurns real turns
decisions.why: The experiment's settle probe (output-settle.txt) shows that a then-callback on a future the test completes runs on a real microtask turn, not through the virtual queue (S1), that continuous outside injection exhausts the turn bound (S4), and that the synchronous refusal inside the zone works (S5). That an async failure from inside the zone would hang is reasoning from Dart's zone rules, not something the experiment ran.

decisions.question: Guide C.4 lists 'capture, replay, and assertion APIs' for the TestBus envelope recorder, planned v1. Is a replay API in bus-testing@v1?

options.label: not in v1; listed under Versioning as a candidate
options.consequence: capture and assertion ship; replaying payloads is a loop over payloadsOf and input that tests write themselves

options.label: replay payloads into a bus
options.consequence: a thin helper over input and stub; little value

options.label: replay envelopes with their lineage
options.consequence: needs a publish path that sets ids, causation and source, which bus-api@v1 does not have and which would bypass Spec §3.11's single-writer rule and bus-api@v1 G12

decisions.chosen: not in v1; listed under Versioning as a candidate
decisions.why: The useful form of replay, envelopes with their lineage, conflicts with bus-api@v1's publish path; the trivial form needs no API. Root D1 cites Guide C.4 for the recorder, so a careful engineer would confirm the narrowing with the owner. Signal that would change it: a devtools or bug-reproduction need, which root D1 puts in v2.

decisions.question: Does VirtualScheduler expose its zone, given that bus-api@v1 lists 'access to the provider zone' as not in v1 for Bus?

options.label: run(body): runs a body inside the zone and returns its result
options.consequence: a test constructs a stub service inside virtual time so its timers are virtual and no settle is needed; the fixtures test the scheduler with no bus; narrower than handing out the Zone

options.label: expose the Zone itself
options.consequence: everything Zone offers, fork and handlers included, becomes part of the contract

options.label: nothing
options.consequence: scheduler cases need a bus to create timers, and shell stubs stay on real time

decisions.chosen: run(body): runs a body inside the zone and returns its result
decisions.why: bus-api@v1's exclusion is about production code reaching the bus's zone; a test scheduler is test-only. run keeps the surface to one method while covering the stub case ADR-003's Consequences describe (a shell service's own timers run on real time).

decisions.question: Does testing.dart re-export the main library or nidana_dart_contracts?

options.label: no re-export: testing.dart exports its six declarations only
options.consequence: one import path per declaration; tests import the main library and the contracts package, as shell code does; pinned by a reject fixture

options.label: re-export the main library
options.consequence: one import less in tests, two paths to Bus and BusConfig

decisions.chosen: no re-export: testing.dart exports its six declarations only
decisions.why: bus-api@v1 decided that the main library does not re-export nidana_dart_contracts; the same rule here keeps every declaration reachable by exactly one library. Close call with no evidence either way; the signal would be consumer feedback on import noise.

decisions.question: Are the recorder's lists live views or snapshots?

options.label: unmodifiable snapshots taken at the call
options.consequence: values that never change under the test's feet; O(n) per call

options.label: unmodifiable live views
options.consequence: no copying, but a list read earlier grows later, and iterating it while a delivery records throws a concurrent modification error

decisions.chosen: unmodifiable snapshots taken at the call
decisions.why: The owner's preference for immutability, and assertion code reasons about values. bus-api@v1's live binding reads envelopes repeatedly and passes on snapshots (T9). The cost is irrelevant at test sizes.

decisions.question: What does a plain Bus do with a VirtualSchedulerProvider, which bus-api@v1's constructor text does not mention?

options.label: it runs on that scheduler, TestBus or not; only a TestBus adds the recorder, input, stub and deterministic ids
options.consequence: consistent with bus-api@v1 G5 (every bus works in its provider zone); several buses, test or not, can share one virtual clock

options.label: ArgumentError: a virtual provider only through TestBus
options.consequence: one way in, but a rule bus-api@v1's Bus constructor would have to state, and a VirtualSchedulerProvider value that is useless outside TestBus

decisions.chosen: it runs on that scheduler, TestBus or not; only a TestBus adds the recorder, input, stub and deterministic ids
decisions.why: bus-api@v1 G5 already implies it, and rejecting it would need a bus-api@v1 amendment for no gain.

decisions.question: bus-api@v1 G38 says nidana_dart_runtime creates no timer or microtask outside a provider zone, while ADR-003 item 6 requires the settle operation to alternate with real event-loop turns. How is the conflict handled?

options.label: state the exception here (G12, G20) and ask for a compatible clarification of bus-api@v1 G38
options.consequence: no consumer is affected: G38 is a source property checked by the runtime's gates, and the clarification narrows it to what ADR-003 already requires

options.label: a settle without a timer
options.consequence: impossible: any await schedules a microtask in the awaiting zone, which is outside the provider zone

options.label: treat it as a breaking amendment and stop
options.consequence: the run stops over a guarantee no consumer depends on

decisions.chosen: state the exception here (G12, G20) and ask for a compatible clarification of bus-api@v1 G38
decisions.why: ADR-003 item 6 is accepted and explicitly requires real turns; G38 restates ADR-003 item 8 without the item 6 exception. No consumer code exists and G38 binds only the producer's own sources, so this is not the breaking-amendment stop.

decisions.question: What does the bus-testing conformance harness supply, and under which runner is the suite bound?

options.label: settle only, as topic-model@v1's harness; bound under dart test only
options.consequence: the cases construct testing.dart's final declarations directly; cases that settle or let real time pass need a real event loop, so no testWidgets binding

options.label: factories for TestBus, scheduler and recorder
options.consequence: suggests a second implementation that final classes rule out

decisions.chosen: settle only, as topic-model@v1's harness; bound under dart test only
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 4 requires a harness with settle; testing.dart has no second implementation to stand in, as with topic-model@v1's value types. ADR-003 item 6 says settle is never awaited inside testWidgets.

decisions.question: Does VirtualSchedulerProvider take its scheduler as a required argument or create one when none is given?

options.label: required positional argument, as Spec §3.6 writes VirtualSchedulerProvider(virtualScheduler)
options.consequence: the scheduler's zone is forked where the test constructs the scheduler, never at an implicit moment

options.label: optional, creating a fresh scheduler
options.consequence: the fork point becomes wherever the provider happens to be built

decisions.chosen: required positional argument, as Spec §3.6 writes VirtualSchedulerProvider(virtualScheduler)
decisions.why: ADR-003 item 5 ties the scheduler's zone to its construction point; a required argument keeps that point explicit. TestBus(config) still creates a fresh one when the config names no provider.

experiments.question: Do bus-testing@v1's fixtures hold together before the producer exists: does every reject fixture report exactly its marked codes, does the surface set analyze clean, does the suite pass against an implementation of the Interface, do bus-api@v1's two bindings run unchanged against that testing.dart, and do the cases fail when the implementation is broken?
experiments.finding: With the stand-in topic model of bus-api-fixtures and a stand-in runtime whose testing.dart implements the Interface: structure PASS for all 20 guarantees (45 cases, 1 binding, 7 fixture files) and bus-api@v1's structure still PASS; surface clean under --fatal-infos; both reject files PASS with their (line, code) pairs (undefined_class for G1, invalid_use_of_type_outside_library and new_with_undefined_constructor_default for G2), so no code is unconfirmed; the bus-testing suite passes 45 of 45 under dart test and a --name '^G12 ' restriction selects its 3 G12 cases; bus-api@v1's surface, reject and behavior files analyze and pass against this testing.dart, and its two bindings pass unchanged, 86 and 43 cases, with the names adopted and deterministic ids (T8, T9); each of 34 seeded defects in the stand-in fails the cases of the guarantee it breaks (T10), no run timed out. One first-draft defect was vacuous and was replaced: swapping runGuarded for run in the scheduler's microtask handler changes nothing, because the SDK's scheduleMicrotask and Timer already bind their callbacks guarded; a zone that swallows errors is the defect that breaks G11. Two first-draft cases could hang a broken implementation (an unbounded microtask loop escaping the zone; a feeder timer left running when settle misbehaves); the loop is now capped at 1000 iterations and the feeder cancelled in a finally block, so a defect fails those cases instead of hanging the gate.

experiments.question: What reaches the virtual zone from a future the test completes in its own zone, with triggerActions alone and with settle; does outside injection exhaust settle's turn bound; does settle refuse a call inside the zone?
experiments.finding: A then-callback registered inside the scheduler's zone on a future the test completes runs on the next real microtask turn, in the virtual zone but not through the virtual queue, so triggerActions alone does not run it (S1); a sync completer runs it at once (S2); a future completed by a real timer is delivered after that timer (S3); a real zero-period timer that injects a virtual microtask on every turn makes settle fail with StateError after maxSettleTurns turns, and settle completes once it is cancelled (S4); settle called inside the zone throws StateError at the call (S5). Work a then-callback causes inside the bus (a reentrant topology publish) lands in the virtual queue, which is why settle alternates triggerActions with real turns.

notes_for_orchestrator: OQ-R2 is decided by bus-testing@v1. Assertion API: the recorder returns typed, unmodifiable value lists (envelopes, envelopesOf, payloadsOf), asserted with ==, Dart patterns and Iterable.where through the runner's own expect (G14 to G16 and the Interface's 'How a test uses it'). Isolation: a TestBus activates nothing, the test activates what it tests and stands in for absent producers with TestBus.input and TestBus.stub (G18). nidana.runtime's decomposition marks the OQ-R2 row RESOLVED pointing at bus-testing@v1 G16 and G18. With ADR-003 (clock control) and root D1 (cross-platform parity out of v1), root OQ2 has no residual left; its PARTIAL row can be swept to RESOLVED by the runtime decomposition or hsdd-reconcile.

Names: bus-testing@v1 adopts every name bus-api@v1's bindings call (TestBus([BusConfig config]); scheduler with triggerActions, advanceTimeBy, pendingTimerCount, settle; recorder.envelopes; RecordedEnvelope.topic and .envelope). No bus-api fixture change is needed: both bindings pass unchanged against the new stand-in (experiment T9: 86 and 43 cases), deterministic ids included. bus-api@v1's Validation sentence 'where it chooses others, its authoring step rewrites the bindings' calls' is now moot.

Compatible, editorial clarifications bus-api@v1 needs (no fixture or consumer change; schedule when convenient, for example at the next bus-api touch or in reconcile): (1) G38 forbids any timer outside a provider zone in nidana_dart_runtime, but the settle operation's real turns are exactly that, as ADR-003 item 6 requires; G38 should except them, citing bus-testing@v1 G12. Until then bus-testing@v1 G12 and G20 state the exception. (2) The Delivery rules say 'the recorder of a TestBus first'; since a recorder attaches to any bus (bus-testing@v1 G14, G17), it could read 'the recorders attached to the bus first, in attachment order (bus-testing@v1)'.

Runtime decomposition: TestBus extends the final Bus, VirtualSchedulerProvider extends the sealed SchedulerProvider, EnvelopeRecorder.attach needs a recorder seam in Bus's delivery path, and TestBus overrides the bus's id generation, so all of testing.dart's declarations live in, or are reachable only from, the src library that declares Bus. The child that owns bus-api@v1's main library should own testing.dart too, landing both contracts' declarations in its first phase. Behavior can then split by --guarantee, for example: the scheduler alone, G5 to G12 (needs no bus); bus on a virtual provider and TestBus, G3, G4, G13; recorder, G14 to G17; isolation and probe, G18, G19. The bus-api@v1 bindings need TestBus and the recorder before any bus-api behavior replay can run.

S12 (navigation-api@v1): resolver wiring tests run on a TestBus with only the resolver topology activated; the auth and policy state topics the resolver reads are stood in for with bus.stub(topic), intents published with bus.input (or an ExecutorSource/PageSource publisher where the source matters), and assertions read bus.recorder.payloadsOf(resolvedIntent). On a TestBus the executor's RouteTransition timestamps (bus.clock.now()) start at 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z and ids are e1, e2, and so on, so expected values can be written literally. The executor-protocol conformance suite is bound twice (in-memory router on the VM, FlutterNavigationExecutor under testWidgets): its harness must not name TestBus or settle, and should abstract time as bus-api@v1's harness does (flush, advance, settle supplied by the binding), because a testWidgets binding runs a production-provider bus driven by tester.pump and never awaits settle (ADR-003 items 6 and 7).

S13 (flutter-binding@v1): the widget-test helpers construct a production-provider Bus inside the testWidgets body, call EnvelopeRecorder.attach(bus) before start() and hand the recorder to the test, and shut the bus down from the dispose of a widget above every scope binding (ADR-003 item 7). They never use TestBus, VirtualScheduler or settle under testWidgets. They import testing.dart (allowed: it imports neither test nor flutter_test) and neither test package. A recorder adds no timer and holds no subscription, so it never leaves anything pending at unmount (G17); OrderingProbe also works there. Widget tests compare timestamps as differences, since the provider clock starts at the test's wall-clock start under testWidgets.

Upstream candidates (decisions above carry the detail; none is marked would_upstream because each resolves a question the Guide leaves open rather than changing the Specification): Guide §10.1's assertion and isolation questions have a Dart answer here; Guide C.4's 'replay' is deferred; Spec Appendix A.7 says only a TestBus records envelopes, while on Dart any bus can carry a recorder.

Timestamps: design decisions carry 2026-10-17T18:01:18Z, the first timestamp taken after they were made, before the experiment was built; the settle decision carries 2026-10-17T18:05:55Z, taken when the settle probe's output was captured; the two decisions made while writing the contract carry 2026-10-17T18:13:42Z.
The replay API (Guide C.4) is recorded as not in v1 with would_have_asked: true (axis); the owner may want it.
